title: Earl Hines's Southern dates and meeting Texas and Arkansas players
summary: Hines's all-black band played the South, where Young met Illinois Jacquet, Cleanhead and Milt Larkin's band in Houston and Al Hibbler in Little Rock.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did Earl's band ever go South?

Oh, we played a lot of Southern dates but it wasn't no mixed band. Oh, yeah. Man, we lived in the South. The first time I met Illinois Jacquet and Clean Head and them, they were playing the Milton Larkins band in Houston, Texas. Yeah. This is early '30's. And they had a good band. Used to -- that was a good band that Milton had. They was blowing then, you know, way back there then. But I met those guys, I met Al Hibbler down in San Antonio, Texas. And then I also met Al in Little Rock, Arkansas. That's the --
That's where he's from -- isn't it?
Yeah, that's where I first met him. But

he used to travel all through the South. When I first met him was in Little Rock. Louis Jordan was from around in there too -- somewhere around in there. But it's just a hop, skip and jump down to Texas from Arkansas, you know.
